title: Can I MASTER the Rosen Score?
summary: Rosen Score challenge site (trophies for Eric Rosen-inspired challenges; he starts at 22/63). Today's challenge: Alphabet Openings - win a game where your first moves spell a word with the files they land on. In the public blitz pool vs ~2000-rated humans he wins 'BEEF' (as black, in 23 moves vs a 2000+) and, after losing a first attempt, wins 'CABBAGE' on time.
rules: Normal chess rules (rated blitz, 3+0 implied by 1:14-1:16 clocks).
Alphabet opening: your first N moves must land on files spelling the target word in order (BEEF = moves to the b-, e-, e-, f-files; CABBAGE = c, a, b, b, a, g, e).
After the word is spelled you may play freely; the challenge counts only if you then win.
win_condition: Spell the word with your opening moves AND win the game (checkmate, resignation or flag).

opponent.name: Online humans ~2000 (e.g. FeFiFoFimothy 2041)
opponent.avatar_description: chess.com default avatar; user shown as Ireallywantcheckmate (2053).

board.theme_notes: chess.com green board (dark sampled (127,164,97); light assumed chess.com default since sampled light square was highlighted), orange arrow annotations. Thumbnail: 'Beef Opening?' with a steak on magenta background.

setup: Standard start; target word chosen before game (BEEF, CABBAGE).
events: Word-spelling progress (each opening move must match next letter)
current_impl_issues: Current 'rosen' mode = trap the queen to win instantly - that's a different Rosen challenge; this video is Alphabet Openings (spell BEEF/CABBAGE with move files then win).
